previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and dysuria, found to have a complicated urinary tract infection likely due to his chronic indwelling catheter. He was treated with intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam after an initial dose of imipenem, with improvement in mental status and resolution of delirium. His catheter was replaced to reduce infection risk, and a new PICC line was placed for continued antibiotic therapy. Left lower extremity swelling resolved without evidence of DVT. Chronic conditions including diastolic heart failure, benign prostatic hypertrophy, type 2 diabetes, and a right renal mass remained stable. He was discharged to extended care to complete a 10-day course of IV antibiotics and continue wound care for a stage II sacral pressure ulcer and penile shaft inflammation.
